judged_text: The all-guests-filtered case throws BAD_REQUEST with the message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' even when the actual cause was blacklisting or already-invited guests, conflating validation, dedup, and blacklist rejection into one client-facing error. Users adding an already-attendee or blacklisted email see a misleading 'Emails must be unique and valid' message; the client dialog likewise shows the invalid-email banner for what is a server-side dedup/blacklist rejection.

record.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The all-guests-filtered case throws BAD_REQUEST with the message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' even when the actual cause was blacklisting or already-invited guests, conflating validation, dedup, and blacklist rejection into one client-facing error. Users adding an already-attendee or blacklisted email see a misleading 'Emails must be unique and valid' message; the client dialog likewise shows the invalid-email banner for what is a server-side dedup/blacklist rejection.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out already-attending emails and blacklisted emails, and if *all* inputs are filtered (`uniqueGuests.length === 0`) it throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`. This message maps to the locale string "Emails must be unique and valid", which is misleading when the real cause is "already an attendee" or "blacklisted" rather than invalid/duplicate formatting. The client (`AddGuestsDialog`) will surface this via `showToast(`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`...)`, so users see that conflated message. (However, the dialog’s red invalid-email banner is only set by client-side Zod validation and is not triggered by this server-side rejection.)
